summary: Iteration 2 — visual redesign + Microsoft Graph email integration fully verified. Backend (pytest, 5/5) and Frontend (Playwright, all 17 features from the review request) pass end-to-end. Contact form submits to POST /api/contact and returns HTTP 200 with status='success' (Microsoft Graph accepted). One UI issue found: on the India-map, the Mumbai and Bhiwandi markers overlap so clicking the Mumbai marker is intercepted by Bhiwandi.

ui_bugs.issue: map-marker-mumbai (x=509 w=143) and map-marker-bhiwandi (x=533 w=155) overlap heavily on the SVG map. Clicking the Mumbai marker gets intercepted by the Bhiwandi hit-box, so office-card-mumbai never receives the active/navy state. Bhiwandi stays active regardless of which of the two markers the user clicks.

issues: Mumbai + Bhiwandi pin labels visually overlap (bhiwandi drawn on top of mumbai). Since Bhiwandi is ~20km from Mumbai on a real map, use a leader-line or a small horizontal/vertical offset for one of the two markers so both remain independently hoverable/clickable.

action_items: Presence map: separate the Mumbai and Bhiwandi markers so they don't overlap on the SVG. Options: (a) move bhiwandi marker ~40px NE with a small leader line pointing back to its real coordinate; (b) render a single combined 'MUMBAI · BHIWANDI' cluster marker that expands on hover; (c) increase z-index and shrink hit-box of both markers and offset one horizontally. Verify by clicking map-marker-mumbai and confirming office-card-mumbai gets the active 'text-white' navy state.
critical_code_review_comments: Presence.jsx: markers for Mumbai and Bhiwandi share nearly identical (top,left) coordinates on the stylised SVG which is geographically correct but UX-broken — a top-level offset or clustered marker is needed.

server.py: /api/contact does not have a rate-limit or captcha, so this public endpoint can be spammed to trigger real MS Graph email deliveries to it.support@vegithglobal.com. Consider adding a simple rate limit (e.g., slowapi) or hCaptcha/Turnstile before go-live.

server.py: logger is defined AFTER _acquire_graph_token uses it (order works only because the log call executes later, but static-analysis-wise the reference precedes the definition). Cosmetic — move logging.basicConfig / logger definition above line 99.

success_rate.frontend: 94% (17/18 items — Mumbai marker click intercepted by Bhiwandi)

seed_data_creation: None. Test contact enquiries were sent via MS Graph as expected (they land in it.support@vegithglobal.com and are acceptable per problem statement).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend /api/contact is fully wired to MS Graph and delivers emails (verified 2x). Use /app/backend/tests/test_contact_api.py as regression. All frontend data-testids from the review request are present (kebab-case). Only outstanding UI issue: Mumbai/Bhiwandi map-marker overlap in Presence.jsx — main agent to offset one of the two markers. All other flows (hero, nav, about stats, WhyUs 6 cards, Pillars staffing panel + facility accordion, Compliance 12 cards + image, Process 7 steps, Industries 8, Clients marquee, ScrollProgress, Footer, mobile menu, lazy loading) pass. No console errors.
rca_of_the_issue: map-marker-mumbai bounding box (x=509,y=9537,w=143) and map-marker-bhiwandi bounding box (x=533,y=9532,w=155) overlap by ~120px horizontally at the same vertical band — because Bhiwandi is only ~20km NE of Mumbai and both markers are placed on the stylised SVG at correct proportional positions with 143-155px wide labels. Bhiwandi is rendered after Mumbai in the DOM (or has higher z-index / larger MapPin+label absolutely-positioned wrapper), so it captures pointer events over Mumbai. Repro: viewport 1920x1080, scroll to Presence section, click Mumbai label — office-card-bhiwandi (not office-card-mumbai) gets the navy 'text-white' active state. Mitigation: in /app/frontend/src/components/sections/Presence.jsx, offset the Bhiwandi marker by ~48px NE and draw a thin gold leader line from its dot back to its true coordinate, OR reduce each marker's clickable hit-box to the dot only (not the label) and let both remain readable.
